questions.question: Rank the following resonance structures of the formamide anion [H-CO-NH⁻ ↔ H-C(O⁻)=NH] in order of increasing stability:

options.label: B
options.text: All resonance contributors are equally stable.

options.label: C
options.text: Zwitterionic / open octet forms < Carbanion forms < N-anion form [H-CO-NH⁻] < O-anion form [H-C(O⁻)=NH].

questions.correct_answer: Zwitterionic / open octet forms < Carbanion forms < N-anion form [H-CO-NH⁻] < O-anion form [H-C(O⁻)=NH].
questions.explanation: Full-octet contributors with negative charge on the most electronegative atom (oxygen) are the most stable contributors.

questions.question: Rank the following carbocations in order of increasing thermodynamic stability:

options.label: C
options.text: Methyl cation [CH₃⁺] < Ethyl cation [1°] < Isopropyl cation [2°] < Allyl cation [CH₂=CH-CH₂⁺] ≈ tert-Butyl cation [3°] < Benzyl cation [PhCH₂⁺].

questions.correct_answer: Methyl cation [CH₃⁺] < Ethyl cation [1°] < Isopropyl cation [2°] < Allyl cation [CH₂=CH-CH₂⁺] ≈ tert-Butyl cation [3°] < Benzyl cation [PhCH₂⁺].
questions.explanation: Carbocation stability increases with hyperconjugation (1° < 2° < 3°) and resonance delocalization (allylic and benzylic).

questions.question: Rank the following carbanions in order of increasing stability (least stable to most stable):

options.label: C
options.text: tert-Butyl carbanion [3° sp³] < Isopropyl carbanion [2° sp³] < Ethyl carbanion [1° sp³] < Methyl carbanion < Vinyl carbanion [sp²] < Acetylide carbanion [sp].

options.label: D
options.text: Acetylide < Vinyl < Methyl < Ethyl < Isopropyl < tert-Butyl.

questions.correct_answer: tert-Butyl carbanion [3° sp³] < Isopropyl carbanion [2° sp³] < Ethyl carbanion [1° sp³] < Methyl carbanion < Vinyl carbanion [sp²] < Acetylide carbanion [sp].
questions.explanation: Carbanions are destabilized by electron-donating alkyl groups (3° < 2° < 1° < methyl) and stabilized by increasing s-character (sp³ < sp² < sp).

questions.question: Rank the following carbon-centered radicals in order of increasing stability:

options.label: B
options.text: Methyl radical [•CH₃] < Primary radical [1°] < Secondary radical [2°] < Tertiary radical [3°] < Allylic radical < Benzylic radical.

questions.correct_answer: Methyl radical [•CH₃] < Primary radical [1°] < Secondary radical [2°] < Tertiary radical [3°] < Allylic radical < Benzylic radical.
questions.explanation: Radicals are electron-deficient species stabilized by hyperconjugation (1° < 2° < 3°) and extensive resonance delocalization.

questions.question: Rank the following substituted phenols in order of increasing acidity (lowest to highest):
questions.correct_answer: p-Methoxyphenol (pKa 10.20) < Phenol (pKa 9.95) < p-Chlorophenol (pKa 9.38) < p-Nitrophenol (pKa 7.15).
questions.explanation: Electron-donating methoxy groups decrease acidity; electron-withdrawing chloro (inductive) and nitro (resonance) groups heavily increase acidity.

questions.question: Rank the following anilines in order of increasing basicity (weakest to strongest base):
questions.correct_answer: p-Nitroaniline (pKaH 1.0) < p-Chloroaniline (pKaH 4.0) < Aniline (pKaH 4.6) < p-Methoxyaniline (pKaH 5.3) < Cyclohexylamine (pKaH 10.7).
questions.explanation: Aromatic conjugation reduces basicity vs aliphatic amines; electron-withdrawing groups further decrease basicity, while electron donors increase it.

questions.question: Rank the following carboxylic acids in order of increasing acidity:
questions.correct_answer: Propanoic acid (pKa 4.88) < 3-Chloropropanoic acid (pKa 4.08) < 2-Chloropropanoic acid (pKa 2.86) < 2,2-Dichloropropanoic acid (pKa 1.30).
questions.explanation: Inductive electron withdrawal increases with proximity to the carboxyl group (C2 > C3) and with the number of halogen substituents.

questions.question: Rank the following isomeric butenes in order of increasing thermodynamic stability:
questions.correct_answer: 1-Butene < cis-2-Butene < trans-2-Butene < 2-Methylpropene (isobutylene).
questions.explanation: Alkene stability increases with substitution (monosubstituted < disubstituted); trans is more stable than cis due to reduced steric strain.

questions.question: Rank the carboxylic acid derivatives in order of increasing reactivity toward nucleophilic acyl substitution:

options.label: A
options.text: Acid anhydrides < Acyl chlorides < Esters < Amides.

options.label: B
options.text: Acyl chlorides < Acid anhydrides < Esters < Amides.

options.label: C
options.text: Amides < Esters ≈ Carboxylic acids < Acid anhydrides < Acyl chlorides.

options.label: D
options.text: Esters < Amides < Acyl chlorides < Acid anhydrides.

questions.correct_answer: Amides < Esters ≈ Carboxylic acids < Acid anhydrides < Acyl chlorides.
questions.explanation: Reactivity increases as leaving group basicity decreases (NH₂⁻ < RO⁻ < RCOO⁻ < Cl⁻) and resonance donation decreases.

questions.explanation: In protic solvents, small F⁻ is tightly solvated by hydrogen bonds; large polarizable I⁻ is weakly solvated and far more nucleophilic.

questions.correct_answer: 1-Butene < cis-2-Butene < trans-2-Butene < 2-Methylpropene (isobutylene).
questions.explanation: Alkene stability increases with substitution (monosubstituted < disubstituted); trans is more stable than cis due to reduced steric strain.
